pillar.name: Pillar 1: Content Intelligence (Source-Grounded Questions)
pillar.gap: Current questions generated by Gemini, but NOT linked to sources. User doesn't know: "PYQ? Phase paper? Official?"
pillar.target: - Every question cites: [IFSCA Reg 2027, Section 5.2, p.180] - Questions ranked by authority: 52% official IFSCA + 30% exam_signal + 18% confidence - FTS5 search: user searches "leverage" → finds related Qs + source links - Week 1: 450 LOC added (question_sources linking + FTS5 indexing + authority scoring)

pillar.name: Pillar 2: Amendment Tracking (Autonomous Regulatory Monitoring)
pillar.gap: Amendments entered manually. User misses crucial IFSCA circular published weeks ago.
pillar.target: - Daily 3am UTC: poll IFSCA, RBI, ICSI sources autonomously - Extract: topic, rule_name, old_value, new_value, effective_date, exam_relevance - Auto-generate 3 questions per amendment - Dashboard: "2 New Regulations This Week" with source URLs - Weeks 2-3: 500 LOC added (amendment_poller + Gemini extraction + auto-question generation)

pillar.name: Pillar 3: Adaptive Mock Generation (Gemini-Native Exams)
pillar.gap: generate_smart_mock() mixes local + Gemini. No TCS iON exam UI. Allocation works but questions uneven quality.
pillar.target: - ALL 50 questions from Gemini (no local fallback) - 60% weak, 25% medium, 15% strong topics - Difficulty adaptive: weak topics start easy, ramp to hard - TCS iON UI: 60-min server timer, question palette, sequential nav, negative marking - Week 3: 650 LOC added (pure Gemini generation + exam UI + scoring)

pillar.name: Pillar 4: Performance Adaptation (Auto-Recommendations)
pillar.gap: intelligent_targeting_snapshot() calculates weakness, but system doesn't recommend next action. User sees metrics, not navigation.
pillar.target: - Real-time weak area detection: accuracy < 40% → "DRILL: critical" - Auto-recommend next action: drill, mock, amendment review, essay, law review - Readiness estimate: "78% likely to score 65+ on exam at current trajectory" - Score prediction based on weak areas - Week 4: 550 LOC added (recommendation_engine + readiness calc + score prediction)

pillar.name: Pillar 5: Essay + Revision Autonomy (Grading + Law Dashboard)
pillar.gap: Essay grading exists, but no daily law revision. No surfacing of amendments/provisions. No full history with citations.
pillar.target: - Auto-grade essays: 4 rubrics (Content, Structure, Regulation, Examples) × 25 points = 0-100 - Daily "Law Revision" tab: high-yield provisions, recent amendments, weak legal areas, spaced review - Full history: every fact traceable to source PDF + page number - Week 5: 650 LOC added (essay grading + law revision engine + history UI)

decision_trees.purpose: Algorithmic rules I (Opus) follow when executing. No ambiguity.

tree.rule: IF feature branch complete AND all tests passing (pytest exit 0) AND no TODOs left in code AND database schema consistent THEN commit with message "[PHASE-X] component: brief description" ELSE log blocker + ask user for guidance

IF acceptance_criteria all passing AND success_metrics at 100% AND integration tests for phase passing (>90%) AND no rollback needed AND git tag created (phase-X-complete) THEN phase complete, proceed to next ELSE identify specific failing criterion + fix

IF error == 429 (rate limit) THEN exponential_backoff(base=60s, multiplier=2) ELIF error == 401/403 (auth fail) THEN use_next_key_from_rotation ELIF error == 500+ (server error) THEN retry_after_60s_max_3_times ELIF all keys exhausted THEN use_cached_local_questions_only + log_warning ELIF circuit_breaker_open THEN wait_60s_then_retry ELSE raise_exception_and_halt

tree.decision: Before committing code, what tests run?
tree.rule: 1. Unit tests: pytest backend/tests/test_*.py --cov=backend -v 2. Integration tests: pytest backend/tests/test_e2e_*.py -v 3. Database: verify migrations reversible (rollback test) 4. Linting: flake8 backend/ --max-line-length=100 5. Type checking: mypy backend/ --strict (if applicable) 6. Performance: latency must be <expected_max_ms ALL must pass (exit code 0) before commit allowed

tree.decision: When do I rollback a phase?
tree.rule: IF breaking_change_introduced THEN rollback immediately ELIF critical_test_failing_after_commit THEN rollback last commit ELIF database_inconsistency_detected THEN run_rollback_migration ELIF performance_degraded >20% THEN investigate + rollback if unfixable_in_30min ELIF user_explicitly_requests THEN rollback ELSE keep changes, log issue for next iteration

error_handling_checklist.purpose: For each task, what can fail? How to detect? What to do?

error.context: Gemini API call during question generation
error.recovery: IF 429: exponential_backoff, retry_max_3_times ELIF 401/403: use_next_key_from_rotation ELIF 500+: retry_after_60s, max_3_times ELIF all_keys_exhausted: use_cached_local_questions ELSE: raise_exception
Return empty array + "No results found" to user

error.can_fail: BeautifulSoup parse error, regex no match
error.recovery: Skip this circular, log warning, continue with next

error.can_fail: Too many concurrent queries, connection timeout
error.recovery: Wait 30s, retry query (PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000 should handle)

risk_gates.purpose: Must-pass gates before proceeding to next phase
risk_gates.gate: All 3,571 source pages indexed in FTS5 TEST: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_chunks == ~36000 ACTION: If fails, debug indexing, don't proceed

Amendment poller completes without errors TEST: Run amendment_poller.poll_and_process() mock, check success count == 1 ACTION: If fails, debug poller, retry
Server enforces 60-min exam timer (no client-side bypass) TEST: Start exam, wait 61 min, submit → expect 403 EXAM_TIME_EXPIRED ACTION: If fails, fix timer validation in submit endpoint
Recommendations generated correctly per decision tree TEST: pytest backend/tests/test_performance_adaptation.py (all 8 tests) ACTION: If any test fails, fix recommendation_engine.py
Essays graded <5 seconds TEST: Submit 10 essays, measure avg latency, must be <5s ACTION: If fails, optimize Gemini call (maybe async)
